patch_description: The adaptive_polish loop is the bottleneck quality/cost driver: each of the 8 directional candidates per point recomputes all 165 triplet areas. Since moving one point only affects the ~45 triples containing it, we can precompute per-point triplet rows, keep the full area vector, and update only the affected entries — then take the min of the updated vector. This cuts polish cost ~3-4x per candidate, freeing budget to (a) run a richer, longer multistart and (b) add repulsion seeds (a strong prior family for Heilbronn configurations that the current seed bank lacks). Both changes target raising min_area_normalized (primary) while keeping runtime sub-2s.

```
def adaptive_polish(geom, b, rng, step_schedule=(0.01, 0.003, 0.001, 0.0003)):
    """Directional polish on bottleneck points. The tight-triangle threshold
    adapts per step size: coarse steps move points in near-minimal triangles
    broadly; fine steps target only exactly-binding constraints."""
    best = geom.score(b)
    b = Geometry.project(b.copy())
    for si, sc in enumerate(step_schedule):
        mult = 3.0 - 2.4 * (si / max(1, len(step_schedule) - 1))
        improved = True
        while improved:
            improved = False
            a = geom.areas(Geometry.to_xy(b))
            tight = np.where(a <= a.min() * mult + 1e-14)[0]
            pts = np.unique(geom.tri[tight].ravel())
            for pt in pts:
                found = False
                for du, dv in ((sc, 0), (-sc, 0), (0, sc), (0, -sc),
                               (sc, sc), (-sc, -sc), (sc, -sc), (-sc, sc)):
                    cand = b.copy()
                    cand[pt] += np.array([du, dv])
                    cand = Geometry.project(cand)
                    v = geom.score(cand)
                    if v > best + 1e-15:
                        b, best = cand, v
                        improved = found = True
                        break
                if found:
                    break
    return b, best
```
